question: 1. How many people are shown holding hands on the Irish Credit Union logo?
explanation: The official Irish Credit Union logo features four stylized figures holding hands in mutual cooperation.

question: 2. What are the three colours of the Irish national flag?
explanation: The national flag of Ireland is a tricolour of green, white, and orange, symbolising peace between traditions.

question: 3. What is the title of the head of the Irish Government?
explanation: The Taoiseach is the prime minister and head of government in the Republic of Ireland.

question: 4. What is the title of the deputy head of the Irish Government?
explanation: The Tánaiste serves as the deputy prime minister of the Republic of Ireland.

question: 5. What is the official residence of the President of Ireland in Phoenix Park?
explanation: Áras an Uachtaráin, located in Phoenix Park, Dublin, is the official residence of the President of Ireland.

question: 6. In which city does the Irish Parliament (Oireachtas) meet?
explanation: The Oireachtas meets in Dublin at Leinster House on Kildare Street.

question: 7. What is the name of the building where Dáil Éireann sits?
explanation: Dáil Éireann (the lower house of the Oireachtas) sits in Leinster House.

question: 8. What is the official national anthem of Ireland?
explanation: Amhrán na bhFiann (The Soldier's Song) is the national anthem of the Republic of Ireland.

question: 9. How many provinces are on the island of Ireland?
explanation: The island of Ireland has four historical provinces: Connacht, Leinster, Munster, and Ulster.

question: 10. How many counties are in the Republic of Ireland?
explanation: There are 26 traditional counties in the Republic of Ireland.

question: 11. How many counties are on the entire island of Ireland?
explanation: There are 32 counties across the entire island of Ireland (26 in the Republic and 6 in Northern Ireland).

question: 12. What is the name of Ireland's national police service?
explanation: An Garda Síochána (Guardians of the Peace) is the national police and security service of Ireland.

question: 13. What currency is used in the Republic of Ireland?
explanation: Ireland adopted the Euro in 1999 as accounting currency and introduced banknotes and coins in 2002.

question: 14. What is the age requirement to vote in an Irish General Election?
explanation: Citizens must be at least 18 years of age on polling day to vote in an Irish General Election.

question: 15. What is the maximum number of pupils on a Credit Union Schools Quiz team?
explanation: Each official Credit Union Schools Quiz team comprises a maximum of four primary school pupils.

question: 16. In the Credit Union Schools Quiz, how many questions are in each standard round?
explanation: Each standard round of the Credit Union Schools Quiz consists of six questions.

question: 17. What symbol appears on the Irish side of Euro coins?
explanation: All denominations of Irish Euro coins feature the traditional Irish harp (cláirseach).

question: 18. Who is the 10th President of Ireland, inaugurated in November 2025?
explanation: Catherine Connolly was inaugurated as the 10th President of Ireland in November 2025.

question: 19. Who is the Taoiseach of Ireland as of November 2026?
explanation: Micheál Martin serves as Taoiseach under the rotating coalition government agreement.

question: 20. Who is the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance as of November 2026?
explanation: Simon Harris holds the roles of Tánaiste and Minister for Finance as of November 2026.

question: 21. What does the abbreviation ILCU stand for?
explanation: ILCU stands for the Irish League of Credit Unions, representing affiliated credit unions across Ireland.

question: 22. What does the abbreviation TD stand for in Irish politics?
explanation: A Teachta Dála (TD) is an elected member of Dáil Éireann, the lower house of the Oireachtas.

question: 23. What is the name of the upper house of the Irish Parliament?
explanation: Seanad Éireann (the Senate) is the upper house of the Oireachtas.

question: 24. How many years is a single term for the President of Ireland?
explanation: The President of Ireland is elected for a term of seven years and may serve a maximum of two terms.

question: 25. In what year was the first Credit Union founded in Ireland?
explanation: The credit union movement began in Ireland in 1958 with pioneer initiatives in Dublin.

question: 26. Who was the Dublin teacher who helped pioneer the Credit Union movement in Ireland?
explanation: Nora Herlihy, a primary school teacher from Ballydesmond living in Dublin, was central to founding the movement.

question: 27. In what year was the Irish League of Credit Unions (ILCU) founded?
explanation: The Irish League of Credit Unions was officially established in 1960.

question: 28. In what year was the first Credit Union Schools Quiz held?
explanation: The inaugural Credit Union National Schools Quiz was launched in 1992.

question: 29. How many rounds are played in Competition A (Under 11) of the Credit Union Schools Quiz?
explanation: Competition A (for pupils under 11) consists of 10 rounds of six questions each.

question: 30. How many rounds are played in Competition B (Under 13) of the Credit Union Schools Quiz?
explanation: Competition B (for pupils aged 11 to 13) consists of 12 rounds of six questions each.

question: 31. What is the title of the chairperson who keeps order in Dáil Éireann?
explanation: The Ceann Comhairle presides over Dáil Éireann debates and enforces parliamentary rules.

question: 32. In what year did Ireland join the European Economic Community (now the EU)?)
explanation: Ireland entered the European Economic Community alongside Britain and Denmark on 1 January 1973.

question: 33. What is the name of Ireland's national public service broadcaster?
explanation: RTÉ (Raidió Teilifís Éireann) is Ireland's national public service multimedia organisation.

question: 34. What is the name of the Irish Constitution, adopted in 1937?
explanation: Bunreacht na hÉireann was approved by plebiscite in 1937 as the fundamental law of Ireland.

question: 35. Who is the President of the Irish League of Credit Unions (ILCU) in 2026?
explanation: Brendan Jenkins is the serving President of the Irish League of Credit Unions in 2026.

question: 36. What was the theme of the 2026 Credit Union National Art Competition?
explanation: "World of Colour" was chosen as the creative theme for the 2026 National Art Competition.

question: 37. Who is the Minister for Education and Youth in the Irish Cabinet in 2026?
explanation: Hildegarde Naughton serves as the Minister for Education and Youth in 2026.

question: 38. Who is the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade (and Defence) in 2026?
explanation: Helen McEntee serves as Minister for Foreign Affairs, Trade, and Defence in the 2026 cabinet.

question: 39. Who is the Minister of State with responsibility for Credit Unions in 2026?
explanation: Robert Troy holds special ministerial responsibility for the credit union sector in 2026.

question: 40. In what month is Stage 1 (Credit Union Level) of the 2027 Credit Union Schools Quiz scheduled?
explanation: Stage 1 (local level) of the Credit Union Schools Quiz takes place annually in early February.

question: 41. In what month is the Stage 3 National Final of the 2027 Credit Union Schools Quiz scheduled?
explanation: The Stage 3 National Final is scheduled for April at the RDS in Dublin.

question: 42. How many seats are in the 34th Dáil Éireann (elected in late 2024)?
explanation: Electoral boundary revisions increased the size of the 34th Dáil to 174 seats.

question: 43. How many members (Senators) sit in Seanad Éireann?
explanation: Seanad Éireann is composed of 60 senators elected or nominated from various vocational panels.

question: 44. What is the name of the highest court in Ireland?
explanation: The Supreme Court is the court of final appeal in the Republic of Ireland.

question: 45. Who was the first female President of Ireland (1990–1997)?
explanation: Mary Robinson was elected in 1990 as Ireland's first female President.

question: 46. Who was the first President of Ireland (1938–1945)?
explanation: Douglas Hyde was selected by all-party consensus as the first President under the 1937 Constitution.

question: 47. What is the name of the "common link" (such as living or working in the same area) required to join a local credit union?
explanation: The 'common bond' connects credit union members by geographical area, employer, or association.

question: 48. Which political party is led by Micheál Martin?
explanation: Micheál Martin has served as leader of Fianna Fáil since 2011.

question: 49. Which political party is led by Simon Harris?
explanation: Simon Harris is the leader of Fine Gael.

question: 50. Under the Irish Government's rotating Taoiseach agreement, in what year is Simon Harris scheduled to resume the role of Taoiseach?
explanation: Simon Harris is scheduled to rotate back into the office of Taoiseach in November 2027.
